channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Flemish climate minister pleased with EU's resilience at climate talks
item.description: While COP31 ended in a deadlock, the proposals on the table were widely unacceptable.

item.title: Marathon climate summit officially ends in stalemate
item.description: This is the first UN climate summit without an agreement in 17 years.

item.title: COP31 has been 'held hostage by oil-producing nations,' says EU presidency
item.description: COP31 is dragging on, having beaten a seven-year record to be the longest UN climate summit in history.

item.title: Falling in love with AI: New documentary explores people's growing attachment to chatbots
item.description: As more people turn to chatbots for emotional support, companionship and even romance, a new documentary explores the increasingly blurred boundaries between technology and human intimacy.

item.title: European-Japanese spacecraft arrives to Mercury's orbit after eight years
item.description: ESA’s Mercury Planet Orbiter is expected to study the planet in detail from an altitude of about 480 kilometres above the surface.

item.title: Zero Waste at COP31? How EU plastic still ends up in Türkiye
item.description: "Plastic waste is one of the most serious forms of environmental pollution worldwide."

item.title: Russian helicopter violates European airspace following drone attack
item.description: Earlier in the day, the Finnish military detected a drone attack on a Russian cargo ship near the Gulf of Finland, in international waters.

item.title: EU sign 'ambitious' trade agreement with Indonesia
item.description: The agreement would scrap tariffs on more than 98% of European exports and about 90% of Indonesian exports, opening a combined market of 730 million people.

item.title: Zelenskyy reaffirms Ukraine's desire to join NATO
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron also called for Ukraine's NATO membership debates to be reopened.

item.title: Finland detects drone attack on Russian cargo ship
item.description: Finland's Ministry of Defence did not disclose who had launched the alleged attack.

item.title: Von der Leyen: 'Russian threats are becoming more and more real'
item.description: The president of the European Commission spoke after an alleged Russian plot to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper in Denmark.

item.title: EUCO President Costa wants to cut EU budget by over €200 billion
item.description: Costa's calculations are therefore even stricter than the budget plan proposed by the Irish presidency last month.

item.title: British minister does not rule out EU membership
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham wants to spend the next 12 months exploring possible models for the UK’s future relationship with the EU.

item.title: Google in bid to buy 50 more hectares for its Belgian data centres
item.description: The plans have already raised concerns over electricity and water consumption, environmental nuisance and the project’s employment impact.

item.title: UN reaches agreement at conference on 'killer robots'
item.description: Human Rights Watch described the results as "disappointing."

item.title: NGO investigates exposure of sensitive data about LGBTQ+ activists on Russian website
item.description: ILGA-Europe, which advocates for LGBTQ+ rights, warned that the disclosure could put activists and partners at risk.

item.title: France's insurers put the cost of October unrest at €207 million
item.description: Damage caused by urban unrest during during October's cost-of-living protests in France could top €207 million, says insurance industry federation France Assureur.

item.title: Riyadh's tallest tower damaged by Houthi strike
item.description: An attack attributed to the Houthi group struck Riyadh's financial district on Thursday, damaging the towering Saudi Sovereign Wealth Fund building.

item.title: Dutch embassy in Kyiv damaged in Russian drone attack
item.description: The embassy is located in Kyiv’s Podilskyi district, just north of the city centre, an area with many restaurants, cafés and offices.

item.title: GTA VI sets several records with global release
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI was released overnight from Wednesday to Thursday on PlayStation 5 and Xbox, breaking several records in the first hours after its launch.
